source_snapshot.procedure: Run dramecc errormode1/injectonuserspace1/mcapolling0/errortype0 without naming a process, buffer, page or target.
source_snapshot.criteria: Tool PASS and corrected OS event within undefined timeout.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic userspace/ECC logs do not prove victim identity.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Requires controlled victim, page mapping, selector binding and data-integrity oracle.

old_problem: The userspace flag identifies neither an owned process/buffer nor how the injector binds a virtual page to a physical slot, so a corrected event could affect an arbitrary workload and cannot prove slot1~N.
disposition_reason: A disposable victim and page map are parameterizable, but the source provides no mechanism showing that `injectonuserspace 1` selects that victim rather than internal or arbitrary memory. This missing proprietary binding is core command semantics and an ownership boundary, not a mere runtime address. ED-16 prohibits injection without it; therefore Pending/BLOCKED remains until AMD documents the victim-selection contract.
decision_basis: Read Reliability row 47, AI fields, historical record 2449 and next pending row 48.
Preserved userspace CE and all-slot coverage independently of explicit-address and UCE variants.
Required a synthetic non-sensitive victim plus checksum/survival evidence.
Rejected NUMA placement or listvalidumc as proof of the actual injected page.
No process memory, page mapping, BIOS/HDT or injection action occurred.

test_case.test_name: AMD correctable explicit-userspace DRAM event per slot
test_case.purpose: Deliver one correctable ECC event to a known synthetic userspace page mapped to each required slot and prove process/data integrity and attributable correction.
required_package: AMD definition of injectonuserspace victim/page selection
Disposable victim executable/buffer/pattern and page-locking method
Profile/tool semantics and per-slot CE timeout/oracle
Abort, allocation cleanup, recovery and BIOS/HDT restoration
test_case.test_command: Do not execute the source command. After AMD defines the binding, create a disposable synthetic victim, lock and map a known page to one slot, bind the injector exactly as documented, run one CE under FAE control, correlate the corrected location, verify process survival and checksum, clean the allocation and restore state before another slot.
test_case.expected_result: The documented victim page on the intended slot receives one correctable event; the process remains alive, buffer checksum is unchanged, the event is attributable and no residual poison or configuration remains.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS exists until the tool proves which userspace page it targets. Generic ECC text, tool PASS without victim identity, NUMA-only placement, unrelated process impact, checksum change or wrong-slot event cannot pass.
safety_gate: Synthetic disposable buffer only; never production or another process's memory.
Freeze ownership and mapping immediately before one target.
Abort on ambiguous victim, wrong slot, UCE, process death, corruption, reset or persistent poison.
No automatic retry; terminate and clean all victim resources.
expected_evidence: Victim executable hash/PID and synthetic buffer pattern
Locked page and physical slot mapping
Full command plus address/location-specific CE record
Process/checksum health, cleanup, restoration and verdict
test_case.recovery: Until the tool's victim-selection mechanism is authoritative, safe cleanup and recovery cannot be guaranteed. The owner must define allocation teardown, poison handling and state restoration with the binding contract.

source_conflict.reason: Memory slot coverage and userspace ownership remain disconnected from the command's undocumented target selection.

blocked.reason: Executing an injector with no proven victim page risks unrelated memory and provides no valid coverage identity.
